analysis.title: Extreme markets: The AI takeover
key_insights: AI dominates US equity returns, earnings growth and investment spending, while most stocks struggle and the economy depends increasingly on a single investment cycle.

The S&P 500 is near record highs, but roughly 60% of its constituents trade more than 20% below their own all-time highs (JPM). A narrow group of mega-cap winners masks weakness across much of the market.

Only around 30% of S&P 500 constituents have outperformed the index over the trailing three years, among the lowest readings since 1991 (JPM). Extreme concentration makes it hard for active managers to beat the benchmark without owning the dominant winners.

GS shows US fundamental long/short net exposure in the 2nd percentile over the past five years even as the S&P 500 trades near record highs. Low net exposure could provide buying power on meaningful dips.

JPM shows earnings across its AI supply-chain basket have risen more than fourfold since March 2023, while earnings among AI adopters have barely moved. Suppliers are monetizing the boom now, and the productivity payoff has not yet shown up in aggregate earnings.

JPM's Cembalest finds that since January 2024, tech-sector returns across major global markets were driven predominantly by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion. This complicates the bubble argument but does not remove downside risk if earnings expectations disappoint.

Investment in information-processing equipment and software accounts for roughly one-third of US real GDP growth, up from almost nothing in 2022 (JPM). Only around 20% of US states are growing faster than the national average, close to the lowest share since 1979.

Since January 2024, spending on data centers and related power infrastructure is up 38%, while manufacturing construction is down 28%, commercial real estate 13% and residential 6% (JPM). Data-center capacity in pre-construction planning has started declining while live and under-construction capacity keeps rising.

Privorotsky argues sovereign borrowing needs are large and AI infrastructure adds a new source of financing demand. If AI projects earn 20-30% returns, borrowing at high single-digit rates can still make economic sense, which leaves other borrowers competing for capital.

The US 10-year yield has been moving closely with selected hyperscaler CDS spreads as hyperscalers shift from generating excess cash to consuming capital. The correlation does not establish causation, but the AI boom may be contributing to a higher cost of capital.

sector_views.rationale: Returns since January 2024 were driven mainly by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion, though valuations are elevated and concentration is extreme.

earnings_insights: JPM AI supply-chain basket earnings are up more than fourfold since March 2023, while earnings of companies adopting AI have barely moved.
JPM's Cembalest: tech-sector returns since January 2024 across major global markets came mainly from earnings growth, not multiple expansion.

risk_factors: Narrow market leadership: about 60% of S&P 500 constituents are more than 20% below their all-time highs.
Economic dependence on the tech investment cycle: a slowdown would weigh on growth.
Data-center capacity in pre-construction planning has started declining, which could signal a shrinking project pipeline. Delays from power constraints, permitting and financing are possible.
Disappointing earnings expectations would remove the support for tech valuations.
Rising cost of capital as AI borrowing competes with sovereign and other borrowers.
vol_and_positioning: GS: US fundamental long/short net exposure is in the 2nd percentile over the past five years despite the S&P 500 trading near record highs.
AI and mega-cap tech are described as increasingly crowded trades, while broader market positioning is light.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech returns since January 2024 were driven predominantly by earnings growth rather than multiple expansion (JPM Cembalest), and AI supply-chain earnings are up more than fourfold since March 2023.
tension_points.bear_case: Valuations are elevated, concentration is extreme, and the investment cycle depends on AI. Earnings expectations that disappoint would hurt, and AI adopters' earnings have barely moved.

tension_points.bull_case: Data-center spending is up 38% since January 2024, and live and under-construction capacity continues rising.
tension_points.bear_case: Capacity in pre-construction planning has started declining, so the future project pipeline may shrink. Power constraints, permitting and financing can delay projects.

theme_stances.evidence: AI can afford expensive money. Much of the rest of the economy cannot.
